---
title: "After the day"
---
A day on data tools ends with a report on your own machine, or a sentence in your notes, and the obvious next steps are the ones that the day only showed on the shared screen: putting the folder under version control, publishing the rendered report, and archiving a version of it. The workspace already carries the workflow that publishes the report once the folder is pushed to GitHub. The day also stops before the robustness exercise of the course, in which you would vary the analysis one decision at a time and send your results to a class chart; the [one-day course on methods](../housing-one-day-methods/index.qmd) does that on the same case, and the [exercise overview](../../cases/housing/exercise.qmd) sets out Tasks 4 and 5 in full. The [companion curriculum](../../companion/index.qmd) covers the material that the day can only mention in passing, in modules that each stand on their own.

| If you want | Read |
|---|---|
| R from the beginning, at a slower pace, on the same data | [Getting started with R](../../companion/intro-r.qmd) |
| The three IDEs side by side | [Positron, RStudio and VS Code](../../companion/ide.qmd) |
| The document format of your report | [Quarto and reproducible documents](../../companion/quarto.qmd) |
| To version your workspace and publish its report | [Git and GitHub](../../companion/git-github.qmd) |
| Where data, code and registrations are deposited | [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd) |
| Every model behind the five reproductions, from a difference in proportions to the logit | [Binary outcomes](../../companion/binary-outcomes.qmd) |
| The whole story of the case, with the sources | [The case study](../../cases/housing/index.qmd) and the [resources page](../../resources.qmd) |

The [short session](../housing-short/index.qmd) covers the same case in two to three hours, and the [one-day course on open science](../housing-one-day-open-science/index.qmd) takes it through reproduction, replication and preregistration.
